All three excerpt sentences present verbatim: PSOC Control C3 family integrating with NVIDIA Holoscan Sensor Bridge to Jetson Thor; 'integration of Infineon's gate drivers and current sensors helps control communication and design challenges in humanoid robotics'; 'full motor control chip set including the company's latest transistor technology based on gallium nitride (GaN)'. Supports both edges (gate_driver + mcu). No numeric claim in excerpt; numberInQuote=false. Trade-press carrying PR claims; portfolio/reference path not proven design win.

WebFetch OK (Semiconductor Today, 2026-02). CRITICAL ATTRIBUTION CONFIRMED: company is Efficient Power Conversion Corp (EPC) of El Segundo, CA — NOT Microchip. Both excerpt sentences present verbatim: 'EPC91122, a high-performance 3-phase brushless DC (BLDC) motor drive inverter evaluation board specifically engineered for humanoid robot joint applications' and 'The EPC91122 is suitable for humanoid robot joints, compact servo drives, robotics, drones, and eMobility platforms'. eGaN power stage confirmed. Page carries specs (20A RMS / 100V / 150kHz / $470) but excerpt has no numeric claim; numberInQuote=false. Evaluation board (reference design), not a confirmed production design win; EPC private (no ticker).

WebFetch OK (Electronic Specifier, 2024-02). ATTRIBUTION CONFIRMED: article is genuinely about MICROCHIP Technology's dsPIC33 DSC-based integrated motor drivers (NOT EPC). Both excerpt sentences present verbatim: 'These devices incorporate a dsPIC33 digital signal controller (DSC), a three-phase MOSFET gate driver and optional LIN or CAN FD transceiver into one package.' and the component-count-reduction sentence. Confirms dsPIC33 DSC + 3-phase MOSFET gate driver + LIN/CAN FD for BLDC/PMSM FOC. Article does NOT mention humanoid robots — general industrial/commercial motor control — which correctly supports the reported_capable_supplier relation (not manufactured_by). No numeric claim in excerpt; numberInQuote=false. EPC<->Microchip split is clean: two separate articles, two separate companies, correctly attributed (Microchip rightly downgraded to reported_capable; the BLDC-for-humanoid-hands article is EPC's, not Microchip's).
